nodes.name: Pyrolysis synthesis of Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC
nodes.procedure: 0.2 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.2 mmol of RuCl3, 2.5 mmol of dicyandiamide (C2H4N4), 0.2102 g of polyether F127, and 2.102 g of NaCl were dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water under ultrasonic conditions for 1 h. Then, the solution was vacuum freeze-dried for 24 h. Afterwards, the dried solid was ground and placed in a crucible, wrapped with a tin foil, and then placed in a tube furnace. The temperature was increased to 550 °C with a heating rate of 5 °C·min⁻¹ under a 10% H₂/Ar atmosphere and maintained at 550 °C for 4 h. After these, the resulting black solid was soaked in deionized water for 4 h, followed by centrifugation. The obtained precipitate was dried at 60 °C for 6 h, resulting in a black powder, which is Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-1. Under the same experimental conditions, Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-2 (Co/Ru 0.3/0.3), Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-3 (Co/Ru 0.4/0.4), Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 (Co/Ru 0.5/0.5), and Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-5 (Co/Ru 0.6/0.6) were synthesized by changing the amounts of Co(NO3)2 and RuCl3 while keeping the amounts of C2H4N4, polyether F127, and NaCl constant.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 exhibits uniformly sized stacked granular morphology with porous surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-synthesized Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 sample exhibits a uniformly sized stacked granular morphology with porous surface (Fig. S2(a) in the ESM)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows carbon nano-hollow structure with uniformly distributed Ru NPs below 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image shows that the granular structure corresponds to a carbon nano-hollow structure with a uniform size and non-stacked carbon layers (Fig. S2(b) in the ESM).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays Ru lattice fringes at 0.205 nm (101), 0.215 nm (002), and 0.230 nm (100); no Co crystal planes observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) analysis displays lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.205, 0.215, and 0.230 nm, corresponding to the (101), (002), and (100) crystal planes of Ru, respectively (Fig. 1(b)-bottom).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals diatomic metal pairs and single metal atoms on carbon layer besides Ru NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition to metal Ru NPs, diatomic metal pairs (indicated by rectangular dashed lines) and a small number of single metal atoms (indicated by circular dashed lines) were observed on the carbon layer (Fig. 1(c))

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS at spots A and B confirms presence of Co-Ru diatomic pairs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their EELS spectra (Figs. 1(d) and 1(e)) confirmed the presence of Co-Ru diatomic pairs.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows evenly distributed C, N, Co, and Ru elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the results of energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Fig. S2(c) in the ESM), Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 sample solely contains evenly distributed C, N, Co, and Ru (Fig. 1(f)).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD shows graphitic carbon (002) at 22.8° and Ru peaks at 38.4° (100), 42.2° (002), 44.0° (101); no DAS peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns of Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 (Fig. 2(a)) show a prominent peak at 22.8°, which is the (002) crystal plane of graphitic carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type IV isotherm with H4 hysteresis indicates micropores and mesopores; BJH pore size predominantly within 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 exhibited a typical type IV adsorption isotherm, accompanied by a type H4 hysteresis loop, indicating the coexistence of micropores and mesopores (Fig. 2(b)).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows graphitic carbon nitride peaks at 480, 537, 613, 680 cm⁻¹; D/G bands at 1344/1585 cm⁻¹ with ID/IG = 0.919.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 (Fig. 2(c)), contains peaks at 480, 537, 613, and 680 cm⁻¹, which are characteristic of graphitic carbon nitride.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of C, O, N, Co, Ru; metallic Ru (Ru 3d5/2 280.4 eV, 3d3/2 284.1 eV); Co as Co3+ (781.3 eV) and Co2+ (782.8 eV), no Co0; N 1s shows pyridine-N, N-M, pyrrole-N, graphite-N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Those with binding energies at 280.4 and 284.1 eV correspond to Ru 3d5/2 and Ru 3d3/2, respectively, and indicate the presence of metallic Ru... two prominent peaks at 781.3 eV (Co 2p3/2) and 796.6 eV (Co 2p1/2) correspond to Co3+, while two broad peaks at 782.8 eV (Co 2p3/2) and 798.2 eV (Co 2p1/2) correspond to Co2+. Notably, metallic Co (Co0) was not observed

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES spectrum falls between CoO and Co2O3 references, indicating average Co valence between +2 and +3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectrum of the Co-K edge for Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 falls between the reference samples CoO and Co2O3 but differs from Co foil (Fig. 3(a)). This suggests that the average valence state δ of Co in this sample ranges from +2 to +3

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge FT-EXAFS: Co-N at 1.48 Å, Co-Ru at 2.48 Å; Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS: Ru-N at 1.53 Å, Ru-M at 2.40 Å; CNs: Co-N 3.2, Ru-N 3.1, Co-Ru/Ru-Co 0.8/0.7 at 2.56 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a primary peak at ca. 1.48 Å corresponds to Co-N coordination... a Co-Ru coordination peak at 2.48 Å... The Ru-N peak is detected at 1.53 Å... The peak at 2.40 Å (Ru-M)... The CNs of Ru-N and Co-N were 3.1 and 3.2, respectively... the fitting of the Co-Ru/Ru-Co pathway occurred at ca. 2.56 Å, with CNs of 0.8/0.7

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs at different scan rates yield double-layer capacitance Cdl = 24.20 mF·cm⁻², indicating largest ECSA among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value (Fig. 4(d)) was calculated based on the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves obtained at different scan rates (Fig. S9 in the ESM). Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 exhibited the highest Cdl value of 24.20 mF·cm⁻², indicating the largest electrochemical active surface area (ECSA)

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistance Rct for Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 among samples, indicating superior electron transfer ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the electrolyte resistance (Rs) and charge transfer resistance (Rct) of this catalyst were examined using EIS (Fig. 4(e)). ... Co-Ru DAS/Ru NPs/NC-4 displayed the lowest Rct indicating its superior electron transfer ability.
